inputs.declared_question: Can the proposed OCI Image Specification adjacency be followed from its current primary sources into exact evidence in Field Note 33 and the public catalog?

external_region.title: Open Container Initiative Image Format Specification

source_facts.claim: OCI Image Specification 1.1.1 defines an image through manifests, an optional index, filesystem layers, configuration, and descriptors, with interoperable building, transport, verification, and preparation for execution as its technical domain.

The versioned configuration keeps ordered filesystem changes distinct from execution parameters and identifies runtime properties such as entrypoint, default arguments, environment, networking, and volumes.
Field Note 33 asks how a browser encounter and public generative work can remain reconstructable after the original catalog, renderer, storefront, and company disappear.
source_facts.locator: What vanished was the building around it: the catalog, the renderer, the storefront, and the company responsible for holding them together.; What would it mean to build a press that expected its own building to disappear?; The browser can perform the encounter on the visitor's own machine.

cartographer.inference: The existing OCI proposal remains a useful technical adjacency for separating payload, execution configuration, platform variants, and verifiable content references. Its container-runtime purpose remains distinct from the browser-readable plate, authorized pull lineage, and finite edition imagined in Field Note 33.
cartographer.uncertainty: The relationship remains model-proposed and technically comparative. It does not imply endorsement, partnership, architectural equivalence, or that container packaging can establish the authority of an artistic edition.
cartographer.attribution: External facts come from the official OCI standards publication and versioned Open Container Initiative repository. Internal facts come from the exact public Field Note 33 source.
cartographer.no_proposal_reason: The bounded source recheck continued to support the existing node and edge proposals. A new candidate would duplicate the current proposal queue.
